title: Equinoxe
label: Polydor
overview:
Equinoxe is a conceptual day cycle — eight parts mapping the progression from pre-dawn to late night. Recorded again in Jarre's Paris apartment, it expands the Oxygène palette with new equipment: Yamaha CS-60 (the warm polysynth central to the daytime sections), Oberheim Polyphonic synthesizer, Geiss Matrisequencer 250 (an upgraded sequencer from the Rhytmi-computer), Korg KR 55 (more sophisticated drum machine than the Mini-Pops 7), and EMS Vocoder 1000. Same recording team: Jarre, Michel Geiss on technical assistance, Jean-Pierre Janiaud on engineering.

Used in Carl Sagan's Cosmos (1980). A 1 million–person audience attended the Place de la Concorde concert in July 1979. UK #11, France #1. ~3 million worldwide. Part 4 is the midday peak; Part 7 is the longest track (7:24) and the album's most cinematic piece. Timestamps approximate to ±5 seconds.

tracks.title: Equinoxe Part 1
tracks.role: Album role: Pre-dawn awakening — the album at its most still and dark. Two minutes of the night before the day begins. Its brevity is the point: night doesn't need long to establish itself when the entire album is about what follows it.

events.description: dark, sparse. The day has not yet begun.
events.detail: The EMS Synthi AKS provides the deep, unstable textures of pre-dawn — not peaceful but not yet alert. The hinge between night and morning.

events.description: a thin, distant sound. Something approaching.
events.detail: Part 1's compositional function: introduce the album's world with minimum assertion. Let the listener's ear rest before the day begins in Part 2.

events.description: the texture shifts subtly. The day is about to begin.
events.detail: At 2:23, Part 1 hands off to Part 2's energised morning pulse.

tracks.title: Equinoxe Part 2
tracks.role: Album role: Morning arrives — the day's first energy. A rising, purposeful sequence announces the working start of the day. The Geiss Matrisequencer 250's tighter, more complex patterns replace the Mini-Pops 7 in the driving role.

events.description: an energised melodic sequence, brisk and purposeful. After Part 1's pre-dawn stillness, this is sunrise.
events.detail: The Geiss Matrisequencer 250 is a step-sequencer capable of more complex patterns than its predecessor — its 12-volt analogue control voltage sequences are more defined and rhythmically intricate.

events.description: the warm, polyphonic voice characteristic of daytime sections. CS-60's distinctive filter gives the morning a golden quality.
events.detail: The Yamaha CS-60 (1977) is a polyphonic analog synthesizer with individual voice architecture. Its filter has a rounder, warmer character than the ARP 2600.

events.description: the morning fills with activity.
events.detail: The concept begins to assert itself beyond mere mood-setting. The day has structure; Part 2 maps that structure's beginning.

events.description: full arrangement at maximum morning energy.
events.detail: Jarre doesn't overplay Part 2. He reserves maximum energy for Part 4 — midday.

events.description: energy sustained but beginning to develop into the more complex late-morning material of the adjacent section.
events.detail: On the original vinyl, Parts 1–4 run on Side One with no gap.

tracks.title: Equinoxe Part 3
tracks.role: Album role: Late morning — more complex, slightly busier than Part 2. The Korg KR 55 drum machine (more elaborate than the Mini-Pops 7) adds a denser rhythmic layer. The day is well underway; this is mid-morning at peak activity before the midday summit.

events.description: the sequence continues in a related but evolved form.
events.detail: Part 3 functions as the plateau between the morning energy of Part 2 and the midday peak of Part 4.

events.description: the more sophisticated drum machine provides a busier, more detailed rhythmic texture than the Mini-Pops.
events.detail: The KR 55 allows more complex programmed patterns. The late-morning soundscape has more moving parts than the clean morning launch of Part 2.

events.description: the Oberheim adds its brighter, more precise polyphonic voice to the texture.
events.detail: Oberheim's synthesizers have a different character from Jarre's earlier equipment — brighter, more immediate. The new instruments signal this album's expanded palette.

events.description: the arrangement grows more active. Anticipation.
events.detail: Part 3's late-section material is deliberately accumulating energy for the Side One climax in Part 4.

events.section: Peak of Part 3 — Side One's secondary summit
events.description: not the album's highest point but Part 3's own internal apex.
events.detail: Immediately gives way to Part 4. The two climaxes are adjacent — Part 3's ending merges into Part 4's opening.

tracks.title: Equinoxe Part 4
tracks.role: Album role: Midday — the album's first and highest energy climax. Part 4 is the summit of the day and of the entire album's first half. The most assertive, driven, and rhythmically complex section on Side One — where the sun is at its zenith and the album at its most awake. Longest track on Side One.

events.description: maximum rhythmic complexity from Part 4's first moment. No build: this is already the peak.
events.detail: The Korg KR 55 and Matrisequencer at their busiest. After the building arc of Parts 1–3, Part 4 arrives fully formed.

events.description: the vocoder processes and transforms vocal or instrument sounds into synthetic voice textures.
events.detail: The EMS Vocoder 1000 had been used to create alien or robotic voice effects since Kraftwerk popularised the device. Jarre uses it textural rather than as a lead voice.

events.description: the Yamaha CS-60 melody is most prominent here, riding over the complex rhythm.
events.detail: Part 4's golden, driven quality — the warmth of the CS-60 over insistent percussion — is the album's most commercially resonant moment.

events.section: Maximum complexity — the album's peak moment (Side One)
events.description: all instruments contributing simultaneously.
events.detail: The Place de la Concorde concert audience of 1 million heard this moment under open sky. Their applause between sections is on the live album.

events.description: the midday sun begins its descent. Energy released gradually.
events.detail: The back half of Part 4 is the afternoon arriving — Side Two will map the second half of the day.

events.description: the energy drops to a sustained level, preparing the listener for the flip.
events.detail: Side One ends at the midday summit's decline. Side Two picks up in mid-afternoon.

tracks.title: Equinoxe Part 5
tracks.role: Album role: Afternoon warmth after the midday peak — the day's energy declining from its zenith but still full of light. Part 5 is gentler than Part 4 but retains its forward motion. Transitional in the day-arc from the activity of midday to the quieter late afternoon of Part 6.

events.description: warmth without the midday urgency. The CS-60 carries the melody with a more relaxed character.
events.detail: Side Two begins at a deliberately lower energy level than Part 4 ended. The sun is past its peak.

events.description: the afternoon's golden light in sonic form. CS-60 polysynth at its most lyrical.
events.detail: The Yamaha CS-60's warm filter character is most appropriate for this time-of-day — richer and fuller than morning, softer than midday.

events.description: contained, unhurried. This is not a second midday but an afternoon that knows its place.
events.detail: Structural self-awareness: Part 5 refuses to compete with Part 4. Its role is warmth, not drama.

events.description: the afternoon fades toward evening.
events.detail: The day is now past its productive centre. Parts 6–8 map the transition into night.

tracks.title: Equinoxe Part 6
tracks.role: Album role: Early evening — the briefest track on Side Two. A transitional section bridging the afternoon warmth of Part 5 to the nocturnal epic of Part 7. As the light fades, the music becomes more introspective and less rhythmically insistent.

events.description: cooler tones, slower harmonic movement. The temperature has dropped.
events.detail: The transition from afternoon warmth to evening cool is achieved through tonal register more than tempo change.

events.description: the melody becomes more inward-looking than the daytime sections.
events.detail: Part 6 is the doorway. On one side: the sunny afternoon of Parts 4–5. On the other: the night epic of Part 7.

events.description: texture thins. Part 7's opening waits.
events.detail: Three minutes is enough to shift the album's psychological register from day to night.

tracks.title: Equinoxe Part 7
tracks.role: Album role: The album's nocturnal centrepiece and most cinematic piece — the longest track at 7:24. Night reverses the day's journey: where the day built toward midday from a quiet dawn, the night builds toward a different, darker climax. Used in Carl Sagan's Cosmos (1980) — the piece that gave Equinoxe its most prominent cultural placement.

events.description: the darkest, most expansive texture on the album. Stars rather than sun.
events.detail: After the compressed brevity of Part 6, Part 7 opens the space of the album to its maximum. Night has more room than day.

events.description: slower, more deliberate than the daytime sequences. Cosmic rather than solar.
events.detail: Carl Sagan selected this piece for Cosmos — the universe as experienced from a synthesizer room at night. An unexpectedly perfect match.

events.description: dense low frequencies, atmospheric washes. The night in full dimension.
events.detail: The album's equipment range at its most dramatic: EMS Synthi AKS for unpredictable textural movement; ARP 2600 for the deeper bass sequences.

events.section: Night peak — the album's second major climax
events.description: Part 7 reaches its summit. Darker and more dramatic than Part 4's midday brightness; this is the energy of the night sky rather than the sun.
events.detail: Two peaks: Part 4 (midday, bright, rhythmically assertive) and Part 7 (midnight, vast, harmonically dramatic). The day and night halves of the album mirror each other.

events.description: the peak energy releases. Post-midnight.
events.detail: The night has done its work. The album moves toward Part 8's resolution — late night into the quiet before dawn.

events.description: the night's last movement. Fatigue and quiet.
events.detail: Part 7 earns its length by covering the most emotional territory. Its 7:24 is the album's most demanding and rewarding single experience.

tracks.title: Equinoxe Part 8
tracks.role: Album role: Late night / pre-dawn — the album completes its 24-hour cycle. Part 8 mirrors Part 1: both are atmospheric and spare, book-ending the day. The album ends where it began — not quite day, not quite night. The equinox: equal darkness and light.

events.description: sparse, tired, still. The day is completely done.
events.detail: The mirror of Part 1: both short (relative to the expansive middle sections), both atmospheric, both near the day's boundary.

events.description: a single melodic voice, soft and resigned.
events.detail: The synthesizers that were assertive in Parts 2–4 are here patient and understated. The same instruments at rest.

events.description: slow chord progression that the entire 39-minute album has been approaching.
events.detail: The resolution is harmonically simple but emotionally satisfying after the journey of the preceding seven parts.

events.description: the last sounds fade. Day and night equalised.
events.detail: The album ends not in silence but in the same atmospheric near-silence as its beginning. The cycle is complete. Tomorrow, Part 1 begins again.
